quiz.q: Which planet has the most known moons?
quiz.fact: Saturn's count shot past two hundred after a batch of tiny moons was confirmed in 2025.

quiz.q: Which letter doesn't appear in the name of any US state?
quiz.fact: Texas and New Mexico cover X, and Arizona has the Z.

quiz.q: Which band released the album Abbey Road?
quiz.fact: That zebra crossing on the cover is a listed site in London now.

quiz.q: How many keys does a standard piano have?
quiz.fact: That's 52 white keys and 36 black ones.

quiz.q: Which car maker's badge features a raging bull?
quiz.fact: Ferruccio Lamborghini was a Taurus, and many of his cars are named after famous fighting bulls.

quiz.q: What does GPS stand for?
quiz.fact: It needs signals from at least four satellites to pin down where you are.

quiz.q: Which singer is known as the Queen of Pop?
quiz.fact: Madonna is one of the best-selling female recording artists of all time.

quiz.q: What's the largest ocean on Earth?
quiz.fact: The Pacific is bigger than all of Earth's land put together.

quiz.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
quiz.fact: And its blood is blue, thanks to a copper-based protein.

quiz.q: What's the fastest land animal?
quiz.fact: A cheetah can hit around a hundred kilometres an hour in a few seconds.

quiz.q: In which country did the ancient Olympic Games begin?
quiz.fact: They were held at Olympia from 776 BC.

quiz.q: Which instrument made Jimi Hendrix famous?
quiz.fact: He was left-handed and often played a right-handed guitar flipped upside down.

quiz.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Au?
quiz.fact: Au comes from aurum, Latin for gold.

quiz.q: What's the capital of Australia?
quiz.fact: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

quiz.q: How many minutes are there in a day?
quiz.fact: That's 86,400 seconds, if you're counting.

quiz.q: Which Michael Jackson album is the best-selling album of all time?
quiz.fact: Thriller came out in 1982 and had seven top-ten singles in the US.

quiz.q: Which of these countries drives on the left?
quiz.fact: Roughly a third of the world's people live in left-driving countries.

quiz.q: What colour is an aeroplane's black box flight recorder, really?
quiz.fact: Bright orange makes it easier to find after an accident.

quiz.q: What's the smallest country in the world?
quiz.fact: Vatican City is under half a square kilometre.

quiz.q: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
quiz.fact: It hangs in the Louvre behind bulletproof glass.

quiz.q: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
quiz.fact: Apollo 11 touched down on the twentieth of July, 1969.

quiz.q: What does a car's tachometer measure?
quiz.fact: It shows how many times the crankshaft turns per minute.

quiz.q: Who sang Shape of You?
quiz.fact: It was Spotify's most-streamed song for years.

quiz.q: What's the hardest natural substance?
quiz.fact: Diamonds are pure carbon, the same element as pencil graphite.

quiz.q: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
quiz.fact: Standard tuning, low to high, is E A D G B E.

quiz.q: Which gas do plants take in from the air?
quiz.fact: They give out oxygen in return, which works out nicely for us.

quiz.q: Which film features the song Chaiyya Chaiyya?
quiz.fact: That famous dance was filmed on top of a moving train.

quiz.q: Which cricketer is nicknamed the Little Master?
quiz.fact: Tendulkar was the first man to score a double century in a one-day international.

quiz.q: How many players does a football team have on the pitch?
quiz.fact: Including the goalkeeper, of course.

quiz.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
quiz.fact: The red comes from iron oxide, basically rust, in its dust.

quiz.q: What's the main ingredient in guacamole?
quiz.fact: Guacamole goes back to the Aztecs.

quiz.q: Which company built the Model T?
quiz.fact: Ford's moving assembly line cut the build time from about twelve hours to around ninety minutes.

quiz.q: At sea level, at what temperature in Celsius does water boil?
quiz.fact: Up a big mountain it boils lower, which is why tea tastes weak on Everest.

quiz.q: Which language has the most native speakers?
quiz.fact: English wins if you count everyone who speaks it as a second language.

quiz.q: Which Queen song mentions Galileo?
quiz.fact: Queen's guitarist Brian May later earned a PhD in astrophysics.

quiz.q: How many continents are there?
quiz.fact: Some countries teach six, by combining the Americas or Europe and Asia.

quiz.q: Which city is nicknamed the Big Apple?
quiz.fact: The name was popularised by a sportswriter in the 1920s.

quiz.q: What's the largest planet in our solar system?
quiz.fact: You could fit about thirteen hundred Earths inside Jupiter.

quiz.q: Which country invented paper?
quiz.fact: Cai Lun is credited with refining papermaking around 105 AD.

quiz.q: Which composer kept writing music after going deaf?
quiz.fact: He was almost completely deaf when he wrote his Ninth Symphony.

quiz.q: In music, what does tempo describe?
quiz.fact: It's measured in beats per minute. Most pop songs sit around 100 to 130.

quiz.q: What's the tallest mountain above sea level?
quiz.fact: Everest grows a few millimetres a year as the plates keep pushing.

quiz.q: Which band sang Hotel California?
quiz.fact: It won the Grammy for Record of the Year in 1978.

quiz.q: What's the national animal of India?
quiz.fact: The peacock is the national bird, so it was a sneaky option.

quiz.q: In ABS brakes, what does the A stand for?
quiz.fact: ABS pulses the brakes many times a second so the wheels keep gripping.

quiz.q: Who invented the windscreen wiper?
quiz.fact: She patented it in 1903 after watching a tram driver struggle in the snow.

quiz.q: Where was the world's first traffic light installed?
quiz.fact: It was gas-lit, went up outside Parliament in 1868, and exploded a few weeks later.

quiz.q: Which country is home to the kangaroo?
quiz.fact: A group of kangaroos is called a mob.

facts: Honey basically never spoils. Archaeologists have found pots of it in ancient Egyptian tombs.
A day on Venus is longer than its whole year. It spins that slowly.
Botanically speaking, bananas are berries and strawberries aren't.
The Eiffel Tower grows about fifteen centimetres taller in summer, because the iron expands in the heat.
Wombats produce cube-shaped poo. Nature is a strange and wonderful thing.
Sharks have been around longer than trees, by tens of millions of years.
The first speeding ticket went to a man in Kent in 1896, for doing eight miles an hour in a two mile an hour zone.
Windscreen wipers were invented by a woman called Mary Anderson in 1903.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
Scotland's national animal is the unicorn. Officially.
There are more possible games of chess than atoms in the observable universe.
A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
The shortest war in history, between Britain and Zanzibar in 1896, lasted under an hour.
The dot over a lowercase i or j has a name. It's called a tittle.
Google's original name was BackRub. Imagine searching that.
The world's first traffic light went up in London in 1868. It was gas-powered, and it exploded.
Venus is the hottest planet, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun. Blame the thick atmosphere.
A bolt of lightning is roughly five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Koalas can sleep up to twenty hours a day. Goals.
One of the world's highest cricket grounds is in Chail, in Himachal Pradesh, built back in 1893.
The QWERTY keyboard layout was designed for typewriters in the 1870s, and we've been stuck with it ever since.
Yesterday by the Beatles is one of the most covered songs in history, with well over a thousand versions.
Astronauts get up to a few centimetres taller in space, because their spines stretch out without gravity.
An average fluffy cumulus cloud weighs around five hundred tonnes.
Ferrari's prancing horse first appeared on the plane of a First World War fighter pilot, Francesco Baracca.
The name Motorola comes from motor plus Victrola, because their first big hit was a car radio, back around 1930.
Octopuses have three hearts, and their blood is blue.
The Great Wall of China is really hard to spot from orbit with the naked eye, despite the famous myth.
Bohemian Rhapsody has no chorus. Not one. Still a banger.
A modern car has around thirty thousand parts if you count every last nut and bolt.

bengaluru: Bengaluru's nickname is the Garden City, and the glass house in Lalbagh was modelled on London's Crystal Palace.
Bengaluru was one of the first cities in Asia to get electric street lights, back in 1905.
bangalore: Bengaluru's nickname is the Garden City, and the glass house in Lalbagh was modelled on London's Crystal Palace.
Bengaluru was one of the first cities in Asia to get electric street lights, back in 1905.
mumbai: Mumbai was originally seven separate islands, stitched together by centuries of land reclamation.
Mumbai's dabbawalas deliver around two hundred thousand lunchboxes a day with famously few mistakes.
delhi: New Delhi was officially inaugurated as India's capital in 1931.
The Qutub Minar, at about seventy-three metres, is the tallest brick minaret in the world.
chennai: Chennai's Marina Beach runs for around thirteen kilometres, one of the longest urban beaches anywhere.
Fort St. George in Chennai, built in 1644, was the first English fortress in India.
kolkata: Kolkata's Howrah Bridge was built without nuts or bolts. The whole thing is riveted.
Kolkata's trams date back to 1873, when they were pulled by horses.
hyderabad: The Charminar in Hyderabad was built in 1591.
Ramoji Film City near Hyderabad holds the Guinness record for the world's largest film studio complex.
pune: Pune was the seat of the Peshwas of the Maratha Empire, who ruled from Shaniwar Wada.
Pune is known as the Oxford of the East for all its colleges.
jaipur: Jaipur was painted pink in 1876 to welcome the Prince of Wales, and it's stayed the Pink City ever since.
Jaipur's Jantar Mantar has the world's largest stone sundial.
ahmedabad: Ahmedabad became India's first UNESCO World Heritage City in 2017.
chandigarh: Chandigarh was planned by the architect Le Corbusier in the 1950s.
Chandigarh's Rock Garden was built in secret by Nek Chand, out of broken crockery and scrap.
mysuru: Mysore Palace is lit by nearly a hundred thousand bulbs on Sunday evenings and festivals.
mysore: Mysore Palace is lit by nearly a hundred thousand bulbs on Sunday evenings and festivals.
goa: Goa was under Portuguese rule for about four hundred and fifty years, right up until 1961.
panaji: Goa was under Portuguese rule for about four hundred and fifty years, right up until 1961.
lucknow: Lucknow's Bara Imambara has a famous labyrinth called the Bhool Bhulaiya, and its giant central hall has no supporting beams.
london: London's black cab drivers have to pass The Knowledge, memorising around twenty-five thousand streets.
The London Underground opened in 1863, the oldest underground railway in the world.
paris: The Eiffel Tower was only meant to be temporary, built for the 1889 World's Fair.
new york: Central Park is bigger than the entire country of Monaco.
Grand Central Terminal has a whispering gallery, where you can whisper into a corner and be heard across the arch.
san francisco: The Golden Gate Bridge's colour has an official name: International Orange.
los angeles: The Hollywood sign originally said Hollywoodland. It was an advert for a housing development in 1923.
sydney: The Sydney Opera House roof is covered in more than a million tiles.
singapore: Singapore is one of only three surviving city-states in the world, alongside Monaco and Vatican City.
dubai: The Burj Khalifa is so tall that people have watched the sunset at the bottom, then raced up to see it again at the top.
tokyo: Shinjuku Station in Tokyo is the busiest railway station in the world, with millions of passengers a day.
berlin: Berlin has more bridges than Venice. Around seventeen hundred of them.
toronto: Toronto's PATH is one of the biggest underground shopping complexes in the world, about thirty kilometres of walkways.
chicago: In 1900 Chicago reversed the flow of its river, so it runs away from Lake Michigan.
amsterdam: Amsterdam has more bicycles than people.
rome: Around three thousand euros a day get thrown into Rome's Trevi Fountain, and the money goes to charity.
edinburgh: Edinburgh Castle sits on top of an extinct volcano.
manchester: The world's first stored-program computer, the Manchester Baby, ran its first program in Manchester in 1948.

Quick one: what are you most looking forward to this week?

How are you actually feeling today, honestly? One word.

What song has been stuck in your head lately?

podcasts.topic: Is it acceptable to sing loudly at traffic lights?
lines: Today's hot seat question: is it acceptable to sing at full volume at a red light, windows down?
Absolutely not. The car is a private concert hall only while it's moving. Once you stop, you have an audience.
Come on! That's the best part. The person next to you secretly wants to join in.
The person next to you is filming you for the group chat.
Then I'm giving them content. Everybody wins.
My rule is simple: if you can't hit the high note, you don't get to do it at the lights.
The eternal travel debate: window seat or aisle seat?
Aisle. Freedom. I can get up whenever I like without climbing over a stranger.
But the view! Clouds, sunsets, tiny little cities from above. That's the whole magic.
You look out for five minutes, then you pull the blind down and sleep on the wall.
Okay, that's slightly accurate. But I own the armrest and the wall. Prime real estate.
Middle-seat people everywhere are listening to this and quietly weeping.
Let's settle it once and for all. Pineapple on pizza: yes or no?
No. Fruit is dessert. Pizza is not dessert. This is basic structural integrity.
Sweet and salty is one of the great flavour combos. Ham and pineapple works, and you know it.
Fun fact: Hawaiian pizza was invented in Canada, by a Greek immigrant. So it's not even Hawaiian.
Which makes it a beautiful international collaboration.
I'll allow it on your half. Far away from my half.
Are you an early bird or a night owl? Because I think mornings are underrated.
Mornings are a conspiracy invented by people who sell coffee.
The roads are quiet, the light's gorgeous, you've done half your day before anyone texts you.
At night nobody texts me either, and I get to stay in bed in the morning. Checkmate.
Scientists do say it's partly genetic, so maybe we're both off the hook.

podcasts.topic: Would you ride in a fully self-driving car tomorrow?
lines: Big one today. If a fully self-driving car was available tomorrow, would you hand over the wheel?
Speaking as a car... I have feelings about this. But honestly, yes, for the boring motorway bits.
I'd miss the actual driving though. The open road, the music, the feeling of being in control.
You'd still have the music. You'd have me. And you could eat a samosa without risking your life.
That's a strong argument. The samosa argument.
I rest my case. And my wheels.

podcasts.topic: Can a cover ever beat the original?
lines: Music question: can a cover version ever be better than the original?
Rarely. The original has the soul. Covers are tribute acts with better marketing.
Hurt by Johnny Cash. All Along the Watchtower by Hendrix. Even Bob Dylan said Hendrix's version was better.
And I Will Always Love You was a Dolly Parton song before Whitney made it huge.
Fine. Covers can win. But only if they're brave enough to change it, not copy it.
The oldest argument in the book: cats or dogs?
Cats. Independent, clean, and they don't need to be walked in the rain.
Dogs are pure joy though. You come home and it's like you've won an award just for existing.
A cat makes you earn its love. That makes it worth more.
Or it's just ignoring you and you've decided that's affection.
Exactly like me with mornings. It's complicated.

podcasts.topic: Is breakfast the most important meal of the day?
lines: Is breakfast really the most important meal of the day?
That slogan was pushed hard by cereal companies, so I'm suspicious.
But a good breakfast sets you up! Without one I'm grumpy by eleven.
Some people do brilliantly skipping it. It really depends on the person.
So the answer is: the most important meal is whichever one stops you being grumpy.
That's the most diplomatic thing you've ever said.
